extracted.intended_audience: USPTO examiners, reexamination clerks, patent owners/requesters, and patent practitioners handling ex parte reexamination proceedings
extracted.subtask_description: Procedural and substantive rules for filing, processing, amending, public access, fee handling, PALM reporting, and examination of ex parte reexamination requests at the USPTO (MPEP guidance).

rubrics_metrics.name: Correspondence addresses and delivery methods
rubrics_metrics.description: All requests for ex parte reexamination and subsequent correspondence mailed via U.S. Postal Service should be addressed to the Central Reexamination Unit (Mail Stop Ex Parte Reexam, Central Reexamination Unit, Office of Patent Legal Administration, USPTO, P.O. Box 1450, Alexandria, VA 22313-1450). Hand-carried or delivery-service submissions should be taken to the Customer Service Window, Randolph Building, 401 Dulany Street, Alexandria, VA 22314.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Requests for ex parte reexamination may not be sent by facsimile transmission (see 37 CFR 1.6(d)(5)). All subsequent ex parte reexamination correspondence, however, may be faxed to the Central Reexamination Unit (571-272-0100). Mark insufficient fee payments 'Mail Stop Ex Parte Reexam' so that the fee may be promptly forwarded to CRU.

rubrics_metrics.name: Identification of reexamination proceedings in correspondence
rubrics_metrics.description: After filing of the request, any letters to the USPTO relating to the resulting ex parte reexamination proceeding should identify the proceeding by the patent number undergoing reexamination, the reexamination request control number assigned, the TC art unit, and the name of the examiner.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This identification ensures the paper is associated with the correct proceeding and file. Use of certificate of mailing, Express Mail procedures (37 CFR 1.8, 1.10) is permitted to file papers in an ex parte reexamination proceeding.

rubrics_metrics.name: Who receives USPTO communications
rubrics_metrics.description: Communications from the USPTO to the patent owner will be directed to the first named, most recent attorney or agent of record at the current address on the Office’s register, or to the patent owner’s address if no attorney or agent is of record (37 CFR 1.33(c)).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Double correspondence with the patent owner and the attorney or agent normally will not be undertaken. Where no correspondence address is otherwise specified, correspondence will be with the most recent attorney or agent made of record by the patent owner.

rubrics_metrics.name: Signature requirement for owner-filed papers and amendments
rubrics_metrics.description: Amendments and other papers filed on behalf of patent owners must be signed by the patent owners, or the registered attorney or agent of record in the patent file, or any registered attorney or agent acting in a representative capacity under 37 CFR 1.34(a).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: See MPEP §2213 for signature requirements. Unsigned papers filed on behalf of patent owners may be returned or treated as defective.

rubrics_metrics.name: Prohibition on untimely merit papers prior to decision
rubrics_metrics.description: After filing of a request for ex parte reexamination, no papers directed to the merits of the reexamination other than: (A) citations of patents or printed publications under 37 CFR 1.501 or 1.555, (B) another complete request under 37 CFR 1.510 or 1.915, or (C) notifications pursuant to MPEP §2282, should be filed prior to the date of the decision on the request.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Any other merit papers filed prior to the decision will be returned to the sender by the Technology Center Director without consideration; a copy of the letter accompanying the returned papers will be made of record in the patent file but the returned papers will not be retained by the Office.

rubrics_metrics.name: Initial processing by reexamination preprocessing staff
rubrics_metrics.description: Opening of all mail marked 'Mail Stop Ex Parte Reexam' and all initial clerical processing of requests for reexamination will be performed by the reexamination preprocessing staff in the Office of Patent Legal Administration, Central Reexamination Unit.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: CRU will perform initial completeness checks (including fee presence) and, if defects exist, notify requester and give opportunity to correct within specified time; incomplete requests may be treated as citations under 37 CFR 1.501(a) or returned if noncompliant.

rubrics_metrics.name: Filing date depends on full payment of fee
rubrics_metrics.description: The filing date of the request is the date on which the request including the entire fee for requesting reexamination is received in the USPTO; or the date the last portion of the fee is received (37 CFR 1.510(d)).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If the required fee under 37 CFR 1.20(c)(1) is not paid in full, the request is incomplete and will not be considered on its merits nor announced in the Official Gazette. Until the entire fee is received no control number or filing date will be assigned and technically no reexamination exists.

rubrics_metrics.name: Handling of insufficient or partial fee payments
rubrics_metrics.description: If no fee or only a portion of the fee is received, the CRU will notify the requester of the defect and give a specified time (normally 1 month) to complete the request. If the fee is not completed, a partial fee will be returned and the reexamination request will not be accepted (or may be treated as a citation if it otherwise complies with §1.501(a)).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If the fee for requesting reexamination has been paid but another defect is not corrected within the specified time, the determination will be made on the request as it then exists. If the fee has not been paid, no determination will be made.

rubrics_metrics.name: Informal request treatment
rubrics_metrics.description: If the fee has been paid but the request does not contain all elements required by 37 CFR 1.510(b), the request is considered informal; CRU will attempt to notify the requester to permit correction before a decision is made.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If the requester does not respond and correct the informality, the decision will be made on the information presented (all art and argument/evidence presented). If the information does not present 'a substantial new question of patentability', the request will be denied.

rubrics_metrics.name: Official Gazette announcement of filing
rubrics_metrics.description: All requests for reexamination for which the fee has been paid will be announced in the Official Gazette (37 CFR 1.11(c)). The announcement will include at least the date of request, reexamination request control number or Director-initiated order control number, patent number, title, class and subclass, name of inventor, name of patent owner of record, and the examining group to which the reexamination is assigned.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Notice of filing will be published approximately 4–5 weeks after filing. Notices serve as public record and may constitute constructive notice to patent owner when actual notice cannot be given.

rubrics_metrics.name: Constructive notice via Official Gazette
rubrics_metrics.description: If it is not possible to deliver mail to the patent owner because no current address is available, publication in the Official Gazette of the notice of filing of a request for reexamination or the ordering of reexamination at the Director's initiative will serve as constructive notice to the patent owner.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Proceedings may continue without actual notice to the patent owner in such instances.

rubrics_metrics.name: Public access to reexamination files
rubrics_metrics.description: All papers or copies entered of record in the patent or reexamination file are open to inspection by the general public and copies may be furnished upon payment of the fee. Reexamination files are accessible via Public PAIR on the USPTO website.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: To access Public PAIR: go to uspto.gov → Patents → 'Status & IFW' → enter the control number of the reexamination proceeding. Copies may be ordered from Document Services Division (DSD) or obtained from IFW via PAIR; certified copies or CD-ROMs are available for purchase.

rubrics_metrics.name: How to determine whether a reexamination has been filed (PAIR/PALM)
rubrics_metrics.description: Use the USPTO website Public PAIR or the USPTO Intranet PALM to check whether a reexamination request has been filed for a given patent number. Ex parte reexaminations are identified by '90' series codes (e.g., 90/005,727); inter partes by '95' series codes.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Public PAIR: enter patent number (no commas), click 'Submit', then 'Continuity Data' and check 'Child Continuity Data'. PALM: from intranet click 'PALM' → 'General Information', enter patent number → 'Continuity Data'. There may be ~10 day lag between filing and PALM entry.

rubrics_metrics.name: TC processing steps and internal handling
rubrics_metrics.description: When a reexamination file is received in the Technology Center (TC): report receipt on PALM, date-stamp receipt, charge file on PALM to the supervisory patent examiner (SPE), forward file to SPE, SPE reviews subject matter and assigns it to an examiner other than the examiner involved in prior examination, inform examiner and enter examiner's name in PALM.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Approximately 6 weeks after filing, the file should be forwarded (messaged) to the examiner and charged to them on PALM. The examiner drafts a decision on a 'special' basis normally within 8 weeks after filing; signed decision forwarded to TC SPRE for review and to technical support for mailing and PALM update normally within 10 weeks after filing.

rubrics_metrics.name: Assignment rule to avoid original examiner
rubrics_metrics.description: The SPE should assign the reexamination to a patent examiner other than the examiner who was involved in the examination of the patent application (see MPEP §2236).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This is to preserve impartiality in the reexamination determination; only rare transfers of the request file should occur.

rubrics_metrics.name: Fees applicable in reexamination proceedings
rubrics_metrics.description: Fees under reexamination include: the request fee (37 CFR 1.20(c)(1)), excess claims fees for addition of claims (37 CFR 1.20(c)(3) and (c)(4)), fees for extension of time under 37 CFR 1.550(c), and fees for appeals, briefs, and oral hearings under 37 CFR 41.20(b). No fee is required for issuance of the reexamination certificate.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Petitions under 37 CFR 1.137 or 1.182 or 1.183 relating to reexamination require fees (37 CFR 1.17(f),(l),(m)). Small entity reductions are available for some petition and appeal fees but not for the reexamination filing fee, extension of time fees, nor certain petition fees (1.182, 1.183). In merged proceedings only a single fee is needed even though multiple copies are required.

rubrics_metrics.name: Mailing/transmittal form for requester address
rubrics_metrics.description: A transmittal form with the requester's address will be used to forward copies of Office actions (and any references cited) to the requester; when the patent owner is the requester, no such form is needed.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The transmittal form removes the need to retype the requester's address for each mailing. Use PALM/IFW to track mailings.

rubrics_metrics.name: Formal requirements and manner of making amendments
rubrics_metrics.description: Proposed amendments in ex parte or inter partes reexamination must be made by filing a paper directing specified changes to the patent specification (including claims) or drawings, and must comply with 37 CFR 1.530 and 1.52 formal requirements.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Specification changes require submission of the entire text of an added or rewritten paragraph, including markings; claims require the entire text of each claim being changed and each new claim; each changed claim should be followed by a parenthetical like '(amended)'; drawings changes require a red-ink sketch and, upon approval, new sheets complying with 37 CFR 1.84 (identify amended figures as 'Amended', new ones as 'New', canceled figures bracketed).

rubrics_metrics.name: Marking conventions for amendments
rubrics_metrics.description: Any changes to the specification, including claims, must show matter to be omitted by enclosing it in brackets and matter to be added by underlining (37 CFR 1.530(f)).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: For paper files use red ink to draw lines through amended claim/paragraphs and bracket canceled claim(s) or paragraph(s) which are part of the patent; substituted copies are indicated by reference letter/number (e.g., A1, A2). IFW entries are made per specified scanning and marking procedures.

rubrics_metrics.name: Status of claims and support for claim changes
rubrics_metrics.description: When there is an amendment to the claims, pages separate from the pages containing the changes must be supplied showing the status (pending or canceled) as of the date of amendment of all patent claims and all added claims, and an explanation of the support in the disclosure for the changes.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This ensures that claim status and basis in the specification are clear to the examiner and will be part of the reexamination record.

rubrics_metrics.name: Claim numbering preservation and numbering of added claims
rubrics_metrics.description: Patent claims may not be renumbered. The numbering of any claims added in the reexamination proceeding must follow the number of the highest numbered patent claim.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Maintain original claim numbering; added claims get successive numbers after the highest existing claim. This applies both to IFW/electronic and paper maintenance.

rubrics_metrics.name: No enlargement of claim scope and no new matter
rubrics_metrics.description: No amendment may enlarge the scope of the claims of the patent or introduce new matter. No amendment may be proposed for entry in an expired patent (other than cancellation of claims), and no amendment other than cancellation will be incorporated into the patent by a certificate issued after expiration.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Although Office actions will treat proposed amendments as though entered, proposed amendments are not effective until the reexamination certificate is issued. Amendments that introduce new matter or enlarge scope will be disallowed.

rubrics_metrics.name: Amendment entry and format requirements (IFW and paper)
rubrics_metrics.description: Amendments which comply with 37 CFR 1.530(d)-(j) and are formally presented pursuant to 37 CFR 1.52(a),(b) and contain required fees are entered in the reexamination file. For IFW: amendment papers are designated by consecutive letters (A, B, C...), entries are blocked and numbered (A1, A2...), marked-up copies scanned into IFW file history. For paper files: amendments are given Paper Nos., designated by letters, red-ink lines drawn through amended matter, canceled matter bracketed, and substituted copy indicated by reference letter.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If a portion of the text is amended more than once, each amendment should indicate ALL changes (insertions and deletions) relative to the current text of the patent under reexamination. See MPEP §§2250, 2270, 2221 for examples and clerical handling.

rubrics_metrics.name: Amendments not legally effective until certificate issuance
rubrics_metrics.description: Although amendments will be entered for purposes of examination, the amendments are not legally effective until the reexamination certificate is issued.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Treat proposed amendments as entered for examination only; applicants/owners should be advised that legal effect awaits the reexamination certificate.

rubrics_metrics.name: PALM recordkeeping and e-File usage
rubrics_metrics.description: PALM is used to support reexamination processing: retrieve reexamination file data, obtain reexamination numbers, monitor movement of files, and record major events. Reexamination papers may be viewed on IFW; status codes for reexaminations are generally in the '400' range.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Within TCs, the reexamination file and patent file are kept together until assignment; after conclusion they are forwarded to the Office of Patent Legal Administration and then to Publications and the Record Room. PALM should be used to monitor major events and to generate tickler reports to ensure special dispatch.

rubrics_metrics.name: Events that must be reported to PALM
rubrics_metrics.description: Major events to be reported to PALM include: determination mailed—denial of request; determination mailed—grant of request; petition for reconsideration received; decision on petition mailed—denied or granted; owner response to determination (owner’s statement) received; requester reply received; mailing of all examiner actions; receipt of owner’s responses and Office receipt dates.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Each reported event is permanently recorded and displayed in the 'Contents' portion of PALM; status representations of these events will also be shown. Reporting supports automated weekly reports and ticklers.

rubrics_metrics.name: PALM weekly reports and tickler responsibilities
rubrics_metrics.description: Various weekly automated 'tickler' reports are generated for each TC to indicate approaching deadlines and processing status. Notable reports: Requests Not Yet Received in TC; Requests Not Yet Assigned to an Examiner (not assigned by 6th week); Requests Which Should Be Taken Up for Determination (assigned but no determination mailed after 6th week).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: These reports are subdivided by TC working group and serve to indicate workload, potential stragglers, and items needing immediate docketing or action to assure 'special dispatch' processing.
